titleStmt.author: >Verna Doherty

publicationStmt.p: This publication is part of the assigned work for the University of Washington class "Texts, Publics, and Publication." Our team chose to digitize selections of "My Awe #8" for people like ourselves: who are interested in zines as counterculture and as representations of artistic and political movements, and who are interested in the form as a collaborative artistic endeavor free of the expectations of traditional publication. We feel that this particular zine represents an interesting moment in Seattle’s political and art history. We chose selections that we believe highlight the patchwork nature of the zine, spotlighting pieces of prose, poetry, political commentary, illustrations, and the front matter, for what they all reveal about the ethos behind the zine’s publication.

fileDesc.sourceDesc:
The zine is made up of a combination of illustrations, handwriting, and type. The font of the type seems to be a Courier font of some kind. The handwriting is usually in all-caps and generally legible, sometimes written in spirals around the illustrations or the typed text on each page. The selections we have chosen are a representative sample of the types of text included within the zine, including some illustrations, pages with typed text, and pages with handwritten text.

Our edition excerpts four items from this Zine:
Verna Doherty "Zero Page"
Verna D. "Denny's Was Closed, A Saga in Portland" 14–18
Randy Strickfaden "Creeping Orwellianism" 22–26
Randy Strickfaden Bruce Storm "Ol' Gory" 27 1985

normalization.p: In our edition, we maintain the distinction between type and handwriting, the incorporation of visual elements into text pages, and typographic features (including errors), which are part of the low-polish appeal of this art form. We annotate the difference between type and handwriting, as well as the pattern the typewriting takes; political context such as local and national government; information about relevant music or art, as best we are able to find it; and what author information we can find. In order to stay faithful to the ephemeral nature of zines, we have decided not to include images in this transcription; we will include the location of where images occur and a description of what they are, but not the image itself.

correction.p: We have maintained typewriter errors and misspellings where we found them, but have annotated such errors. We did not maintain line breaks in prose, so anytime that there is a word sepreated by a hyphen, we replaced with the full word; this is marked with tag.

segmentation.p: We digitized the following sections: “Page Zero” by Verna, “Denny’s Was Closed, A Saga in Portland” by Verna D. (pp.14-18); “Creeping Orwellianism” by Randy Strickfaden (pp.22-26); and “Ol Gory” by Randy Strickfaden and Bruce Storn (p.27, 1985)

profileDesc.creation: This zine represents much of the rhetoric and aesthetics of what would be known as the Grunge movement, which has its origins traced to Seattle in the 1980s. References are made to punk and grunge bands, musicians, and locations of the era. The political commentary of the zine often either directly or indirectly addresses the reader with the intent of expressing frustration or warning about the governments and institutions the zine is pushing back against.

div.p: Seattle, Washington has long been a center of counterculture in the United States, especially for the grunge rock scene in the 1980s and 1990s, which was sometimes called the "Seattle sound". The zine "My Awe #8: The Winter Desperation Issue" emerges from this culture in winter 1987. Published by a variety of creators, it includes information about the local music scene, including pamphlets and concert dates; personal narratives of attending and planning concerts; political commentary in the form of poetry and essay; and more. This piece provides an excellent overview/sampling both of the kinds of writing and affiliations from this period and of the contents of zines more generally.

Zines are a form of independently published publication that often represent countercultural movements or ideas. "Often the work of one author and either free or nominally priced, zines offer an intensely personal, highly affordable, and often subversive method of independent grassroots communication". Originating in the science fiction community as "fanzines," the form was taken up by the hardcore-punk music scene in the 1980s and 1990s, when “My Awe” was created. As a group, we are fascinated by the counterculture ethos of zines and seek to represent this one in a way as consistent with the principles of its creators as possible.

Because of this desire to remain consistent with the ethos of this zine, our team is navigating an ambivalence towards the idea of publishing this content in digital form, concerned that circulating it outside of its context might contribute to the larger trend of co-opting and incorporating countercultural trends into mainstream culture. Our selections and editorial choices therefore represent only a small sample of the zine, with identifying information such as phone numbers censored (though the numbers are unlikely to still be in service). We also chose to digitize selections that we feel best represent the community and artistic connections of the zine (the "Zero Page"), the diversity of its content (two different prose pieces and one poem), the political commentary that zines allow ("Creeping Orwellianism" and "Ol' Gory"), and the personal stories of those involved in the scene ("Denny's Was Closed, A Saga in Portland"). When possible, we have retained formatting mistakes and typewriter errors , to best represent the homemade nature of the publication. We have also distinguished between handwriting and type, as the zine involves both.

div.head: by Verna D.

hi.hi:
There was this young woman who thought she could, you know, take on, not the world, but a thing/something in her gut drove her to do it/what was it? No one knows
for sure just what it was/Most of the time she felt lonely and much like an outsider, never fitting in, though she tried, not to get in, but just make peace for once
be accepted as she was/Of course this never happened/Close but no . . . And the times it was close/enough so she could touch it/she got scared and ran away/no one knows why/another instinct perhaps or her head just kind of got fucked up/Anyway, this thing she decided to do—it was never clear in her mind how to go about doing it/She knew the basics but
something got in the way/She invited failure like it, too, was a drive/She failed at the thing/Not failed in the thing itself but things surrounding the thing/Can anyone understand/Until they see/Again, she was rejected/Back to the normal state of affairs/And it's hard to see, so hard to see/She didn't want anyone to know/her fears/They can't know/But she let it out anyway/Why? "It's only pain, it doesn't hurt" WH

div.p: This is a true and actual (if not always factual) account of my experiences during the weekend of the 7 SECONDS shows,one of which I co-promoted. Some of this information is taken directly from my journal entries at that time. Other parts are embellishedjournal pieces, or taken from memory and filled in as I go now.

I decided to leave out some stuff,because it is too personal for this 'zine, or inappropriate and/or incriminating. Mostly, it is just a personal account of my thoughts at that time, which began Oct 18th, 1986, and ended Oct. 19th (or 20th,actually.). So here goes nothing:
div.ab: SATURDAY, OCT. 18th, PART ONE — CARRIDE TO OLYMPIA,FROM PORTLAND.
div.p: Coffee. The initial buzz is good.My eyes are out and shining . Lucid. No towel,no shower — no dice. I feel like a scummy heap o' NO USE.NO use for me today. Hangin' around like a noose around someone's neck. I hate relying on people.I would rather rely on myself.By the same token I would rather rely on acquaintences than friends,and much better rely on total strangers. I can't get pissed at friends or acquaintences if they disappoint,because I feel bad or guilty or stupid. But strangers can fuck off if they cross me in some way,and I won't care.

This is odd man out time. Talking, acting like I know what I'm doing when in actuality, I feel completely lost inside. Acting tuff,like I'm a big shit,but I totally have no clue.None at all.Big talk but I'm scared. Feeling pretty self-righteous. This is an honest(defensive) feeling but dangerous...
Bad sleep lately.

I want to stare at the sun until I learn to see. Something like that. If I stare at the sun on Hank's back,will it have the same effect?(I been readin' Rollins' Hallucinations of Grandeur, on the way down here Friday, and it stuck in my haid)...
I'm bummin'. I don't know why. Not really as "up" for the show as I would like to be. At this point , I will settle for a few recognizable faces.

p.hi: (Stopped at a Chehalis,WA gas station/askin' directons to a skate park/I joke about the small hicktown whiteness of the place/"take a left at the crossburnin'"/ this has me goin' even after we leave the place...)

div.p: I'm so witty.Pass the chloroform.O.K. Carrying only one tape with me — Flipper Blown' Chunks . Pass the ludes.No seriously.I'm swelling up, gettin' too big for my britches.Cracks,cracks and more cracks. Mouth full of shit.Head full of shit. Riding in this car.With this girl and this guy. How do I know I can trust 'em. How do I know they won't drop me off in Chehalis? And book. Or bail.Book, that's a word used when I was in jr. high school, meaning leave a place. There are so many words for leaving . So many ends to a mean (a way).One mean can have a thousand ends.More than I can think about. I wouldn't write this if I weren't on the road...(on heavy drugs, haha)... when I close my eyes and let the music in it cuts deep. It hurts and feels good all at once...

lg.l: There are thousands of highways
And thousands of visions
There's more than a million veins
needing to be fed
Hungry for blood(traffic)
Dusk snuggles in and waits
For the dance of darkness to begin
The word dusk reminds me of the word dust
And dust remind s me of the underside of my shell
Which badly needs shaking out

div.p: (Flipper intones on the car's tape player) "WE ARE BREEDING"
Darkness coming on as tape advances to my favorite Flipper songs. "In Your Arms",followed by "Life is Cheap."
Night has left me hollow.

(Finally here. all right . Startin' to warm up a bit and get a little excited. So I go to the door ,or where they take your money,and I go, "I think I'm on the guest lis". I'm not,but they let me in anyway,because I tell them I'm promoting the Portland show. I guess that was o.k. to do...I don't know. I missed most of Danger Mouse visiting with the Yobs. I barely recognize anybody, and make lots of stupid cracks ,generally being a jerk. Out of sheer nervousness I think.Yeah. What I saw of Danger Mouse I really ,really liked. For one thing, Kurt is an awesome performer, and him and the whole band were fun to watch. I was pretty distracted, which is understandable because of lack of sleep ...Back to the journal.)

Melvins real hot tonight.Smokin' long songs sendin' shivers in me.Woa. By the stage writing. No headbangin'. Neck sore from last nightss Saccharine Trust show. Feelin' just a little bit sick. Don't know why. Just a little.
So full of shit last night I thought I would scream. I thought someone would get wise and beat the crap out of me.

Unseen Force were good. Yobs were happening.7 Seconds were hot. Sets were too short. A guy dove off the stage and busted his head maybe. He's like , "Fuck you! I don't want to go to the hospital!" (His choice was either go with the medics or with the cop. Now which would you choose?)
Did Stan ( promoter of the show in Olympia) do okay? I wonder.
div.ab: 8:40 a.m. Sunday.Sleep okay.Not good yet.When will it be? I wonder. I told the bands their soundchecks were at 2 and 3,etc. Fuck is the sound even gonna be there?That would be kind of stupid if it weren't.
div.p: This place, this place is a castle. Jeannie and Steven's place is rather the cool spot. Nice. Plushy almost.Roomy enough to hold all three bands. No,not really. Want to get to talk more with Kevin, but why?

The best stuff is what I leave out of the journal. Crap. Invited Jennifer and Kris to the show. Kris won't make it and Jennifer will forget. I feel crummy for lying to her. I lied so much last nightf. I'm just a liar. Panik was there. Good.

I look in the mirror and I hate what I see. I hate what I see ,and can almost like what I hate. I look sick,stupid,and lame.I feel strong ,absorbant,reliable, like a human tampon or paper towel. Kinda bummin'. Fuck! Why!?I feel stupid here, "turning even less than stupid..." Ahahahahahahaha.
div.ab: PART THREE — THE SHOW. BEFORE AND AFTER.
div.p: ( This whole thing is written from memory,because I had no time or desire to write in my journal at this time.If it seems fragmented, it is justifiably so, for this is being penned months after the fact.All right?)

The confidence of last night did not carry over to today,the stupidity did. Shouldn't I be doing cocaine or something.? I do not feel like a gonzo promoter at all, and this is a very scary,definitely destructive feeling. Steven is busy doing things, and I'm just sort of sitting here in this huge place, cleaning up a leftover mess because I don't know what else to do.

The Rebel Skates crew is already here,set up for the skate competition. I was worried it was gonna rain,but it's actually a pretty nice day out. There seems to b e a lot of kids for the competition, I wonder if they will all come for the show.

Off to find some food. All they had that I could afford was these greasy fries, hardly a gastronomical delight. Oh well, I need my energy, and it looks like there won't be any coke (or even Pepsi.) So, anyway, this place is pretty cool, think I'lkl l hide out in the band room for a while.

Shit! They announced the contest,telling the skaters they can get in for free with the $4 entry fee to the contest! Fuck, it's s'posed to be the other way around,I thought I made that clear, but oh well.Well, this is just dandy. Where is the money from the show going to come from? Fuck it all to hell.I really don't feel in control now,but Steven (co-promoter) seems to have everything pretty much taken care of.

Well, it kinda sucks that I can't go in the Monqui office ,and that they (Monqui) won't listen to me and will listen to Steven,but they don't really know me, and he works for 'em. So, I paid them (it still sucks). The guy that was supposed to clean never showed up so I just did what I could. It wasn't that gruesome. Things seem to be going wrong left and right. Everyone's late pretty much. At least the sound is here. Maybe they aren't late. The Yobs showed up early and 7 Seconds were pretty much on time, just my Seattle friends were late. Oh well,it's okay.
7 Seconds sounded great in the soundcheck. That woman doin' the sound is great. The sound here is awesome. Loud enough, vocals clear, just great! It's gonna be a good show, if everyone shows up .

Well , all the bands are here,but where are the Fallen Angels. They were supposed to be here an hour ago. Maybe they got a late start.Shit, the doors are supposed to open now. I feel like a complete jerk. My security didn't even show up. What the fuck,the show must go on without them. It's good that some Monqui people,or Steve's friends,are here (thanks Bruno, thanks >Bill and others!) or I would be dead.I'm not even worried about the skate thing anymore,too busy worrying about the Fallen Angels not being here. I'm a wreck. Safe in this ticket booth I guess. There seems to be a lot of kids waitin' to get in. That's cool! I'm sellin' lots of tickets which is good, and it seems like most of the skaters are
comin' in too. Great! Ah relief,the Fallen Angels got here finally. I am not mad at them, just exasperated in a way...

Well, I"m missing all the bands sittin' out here in this booth. Bruce is here to keep me company and that is great. He is the only stabilising force around me right now , and I can't say how much of a great comfort that is to me. He even bought me an ice tea! What a pal!

Looks like at this preliminary count that I'm about three hundred or more in the hole. The prospect is grim. The show's almost over and it doesn't look like there's going to be many more people showin' up. 7 Seconds is going to be on soon.Some folks comin' in are mad that it's still five dollars. It's not my fault they are late. They don't know I'm in the hole and need every cent I can get to pay everyone off...

I ran out into the room twice during 7 Seconds' set. Once for "Just One Day!" and once for "Somebody Help Me Scream". That was really fun,k intense, awesome, just lettin' loose and dancing and shouting along to those songs. It meant so much to me right then and there, moreso than at any other time that whole day. It was magic,just beautiful.

By the end of the eveningg I felt really, well, insecure. I felt that I had done all the wrong things, that the whole problem centered on what I personally fucked up. I felt bad that I couldn't pay the Yobs what I had promised them, but they were pretty good natured about it. It was fun to hang out with the bands and just listen and feel almost like we were friends, or something silly like that. There are many things I wanted to ask and say, but held back because, well, I don't really know these people, except through their music/ Sometimes I wish I could just express, without fear, what I am thinking, what I am feeling, at the exact moment I am thinking it. Perhaps I would have been better off a drunken groupie, I don't know.

Dennyss was closed ! What?! Yes , that's right, three carloads of people(four carloads?) Like, eighteen fuckin' possible customers and the damn place is closed! I am feeling so strange ,so , just like I'm in a dream or a bad new wave movie.We all want to go congregate somewhere , so , oh, let's just go on the highway and head south. I'm hoping we don't end up in Salem.

We all come to rest at Bob's Big Boy,in Wilsonville,OR.Not a big town. The poor waitress. All of a sudden ,here's thes e people, not g quite what they expected I'll bet. These scraggley, hardcore,not-so-hardcore, not-so-scraggly, pretty boisterous, group of folks. Oh, okay. She handled it pretty well and the scarier people were served by the manager! These kids were mighty hungry. Obligatory Yobs/7Seconds food fight,stolen silverware(okay,so I was feeling desperate!). Lucky for the Bob's Big Boy crew we didn't stay very long.

Obligatory Yobs sendoff/goodbye after the Bob's destruction and thievery. Hugs and kissies and off we all go into the wild night... (And my prose falls apart). WE get in our respective vehicles and mosey on down the highway, Yobs on their way home, and the rest of back to Steve and Jeanniess for rest and chatter.then , sleep.
(end of memory-writing,back to journal)

I lost my shirt,and my pants and my shoes and socks. Itcs hard to let it all sink in.I don't like people much right now.But then I'm sure they like me even less. It's here that my writing falls apart.I'm hittin' the burnin' stuff(vodka) and feel like I don't know who I am really.I never have.Don't know if I ever will.Should I leave.(over at Jeannie and Steven's house/feeling uncomfortable)I kinda want to. The reading tomorrow should be real good,leaving me emptier than ever. I sort of understand,but I don't know. Who do I have to talkk to?No one really knows what's going on inside my head.No one wants to. I know I don't. Lucidity is a lie. I'm susceptible.Hurtin' Haha. O.k., now wait a minute there.Hold on a second.Feeling divorced.Alienated.

Early morning smog walk to Quality Pies was good. The smog is rich.I like it because it allows me to hide.I especially dug it last night. So (around 5 a.m.) I'm in the Q.P. and order a baked potato.I attempt to anyway, but my voice is gone, so the order is a faint whisper, right. So, I'm writing theis letter to Kevin,which became dotted with butter,thinking suicidal as I write,no,but he doesn't need to hear my ramblings at a late nite/all nite diner,foggy from lack of sleep... Augghhh! Had to bail from this house. Nothing to lose.
I'm ugly today.Good.Will keep the assholes away.(?) When will I come to an understanding. When will they come to an understanding of me?Never.

Beautiful day out.Children yelling their guts out at Couch Park.The fall leaves remind me of what is right with the world . The smell of their decay fills the air. That smell specific to Autumn. A smell I'm very fond of.
Members of radical organization chant anti-U.S. slogans and burn a mock American flag.

lg.l: See ol gory waving high,
In uh sun tanned land against blue sky.
Three colors, stars, and stripes no more,
to honor the heroes who die in war.

Dust to dust, ashes to ashes, and some mumbo jumbo
about the lord.
If you ask me, uh mighty piss-poor sorta reward.
Mt. RushNomore to have got nowhere,
at so their stone faces stare.
Plastic surgeons rush to rescue lady lib.
The bottom's breakin' out of this crib.
One nation under uh thousand competitive gods in confliction,
with their will to power being the cause of our affliction.

And of course it's all just uh lotta baloney, but see um
there at the ceremony- shake hands with one another,
pretending to be uh patriotic brother.
Meanwhile, here is me in this rich country
with an ocean on each side.
Here is me in this rich country
left with little pride.
And on either side of all that water,
I know, I know, there's nothing any hotter.
This here lands the best there is no matter where ya go.

This here lands the best there is, I guess that's what
depresses me so.
You see, along the way ol gorys been stained by the certain

things it did, and instead of facing up it only ran and
hid.
You see, right now ol gorys being stained by the certain

things it does, it's being brought back to the way of
which it was.
O1 gorys getting stained as it moves backward in its track.
O1 gorys becoming so stained its turning black.
But will it ever do the certain things it needs to,

the opposite of what it has, so as, to wipe it all
clean?
Just to stop is not enough. But will it
ever do what it needs to remains to be seen.

They bomb this group of people whom for so long have not had the chance to live conceptually, nor any other way free, for hundreds of years governed by coercive rule which has served to form their warped mentality. faster rate. And further I note, the publics' revenue they have stole away from me and you, and used it for their own pet projects which, believe me, don't do us any good, and have ignored their true responsibility of office, whereas, otherwise it MIGHT have been used as it should.

When it comes to representing the people, I ask: is this present leadership our best choice? Does it really represent the peoples' voice? Those who with out precious environment will protect from further damage, and be ethical at using their know-how to responsibly manage. Those who will adequately defend the nation's ground while will still work to make relations between us and other countys not as tense, and who to their defense contractor buddies wont be throwing the money all around at the taxpayers' expense. Those who will not lie, but instead address the true issues of out time; the ones of the most relevance. Those who are, oh yea sure full of love, peace, and vision, but much more so than that capability and intelligence. Those who use diplomacy, negotiation, and cooperation as their tools when amongst ourselves or with others we get into uh fix, and will do their damnedest to keep us out of any violent conflicts. Those who with out world neighbors--the citizens of other states--will not intervene in what is really their affair for not the slightest length of duration, and will instead respect these peoples' sovereign right to self-determination. Those who through some half-assed mediocre way will at least use our money in an attempt to do good deeds by supporting programs for society; things that everybody needs. Instead of for some nuclear reactor where we the people are in no way the real benefactor, or for increasing the chances of annihilation everywhere so that everything may soon be gone, they will funnel the bucks toward desperately needed education, healthcare, and so on.

Yep, if we're ever fortunate enough to once again get those "do-gooders" back, of course we should feel beter for the time while our itch is gettin' scratched, but we shouldn't feel so damned good that we start countin' out chickens before they are actually hatched. For
then will not be the time to forget, relax, and concern ourselves once again with only havin' fun, for then will be the time to get some change for the better kind of work once and for all done. Perhaps we can revise the system in a way which will make out democracy more foolproof, and will serve to eliminate the financial support from greedy slobs backing any ol' incompetent goof. I say create a political process which is bound by a code of ethics, and discipline to be enforced by a constitutional mandate. And for the purpose of insuring capability, set intellectual prerequisites for every candidate. Let's revise out democracy in a way where we all can be glad. Once changed for the better so as to protect us from any big brother whom would run for office wishing to do bad.

But for now it looks like we're stuck with this one, and it offers us few preventions that those with bad intentions will not ascent to the seats of power so that in them we the people have sit "creeping Orwellions" who for me and you care not one single bit, and are themselves for this job not at all fit.

And what's the result for all of us? What is our reward? Well let's celebrate, time to pour the champagne, just like the president promised throughout his campaign we get ta see um bring America back, but never move 'er forward.

div.note: In deciding what to publicize and whether to publicize it, we are aware of the tendency of more formal publishing to co-opt underground (and often very personal) cultural objects such as zines, bringing them into mainstream culture and thereby both robbing them of their subversive power and exposing those who participate in these movements. Ann Japenga writes about the mainstream co-optation of Riot Grrl culture, arguing that “An authentic counterculture is as necessary to the larger society as the rain forest is to the planet. It's a protected laboratory where evolution can take place.” She writes about Riot Grrls crying over the exposure of their privacy and the secrets they shared in their zines. Although several decades have passed since this zine was created, and it is now closer to a historical artifact than an immediate revelation, we try to maintain this ethos in our editorial choices. For this reason, we have chosen to censor personally identifying information such as phone numbers. (However, we have retained addresses that lead to PO boxes, as we imagine those are not directly associated with specific people.)

"Creeping Orwellianism" is a political prose piece/rant about invasive drug testing policies. It is likely a reference to the Anti-Drug Abuse Act of 1986, which was "the Reagan Administration’s response to a national moral panic around crack cocaine" and drastically increased criminalization of drugs, which has contributed to mass incarceration (Lipke)

"Ol Gory" is a politically charged poem criticizing what was then the current state of US militarism and nationalism. The name "Ol Gory" is a play on words for the term "Old Glory," as in the flag of the United States. The imagery portrays the staining of the flag through the wrongdoings of the American Government. In many radical eyes at the time, America was no longer the leader of the "free world," but rather a "fanatically capitalist power, willing to follow militarist policies of nuclear intimidation and conventional military intervention to protect its politico-economic interests".

In the case of typewritten or handwritten text in which one letter was typed or written on top of the previous, however, we have read the word as we assumed it was meant to be written for simplicity's sake.

In the physical layout of "Denny's Was Closed, A Saga in Portland," each page is mostly typed, but includes handwritten prose in spirals around the page.re To represent this in TEI, we have placed all the handwritten text together in a section at the beginning of the entry with page breaks entered into it to indicate which page it surrounds.
"Lude" here is likely referring to a pill of methaqualone, a sedative. The term is short for Quaalude, a brand name for methaqualone.
